newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish yields undaunted by budget gap, seen flat.
newsitem.headline: Polish yields undaunted by budget gap, seen flat.

text.p: Yields of Polish T-bills are seen holding relatively flat at Monday's 950 million zloty primary tender as markets keep cool amid talk of higher 1997 inflation and a larger-than-expected budget deficit.

Analysts forecast on Friday bids at next week's tender would nearly double the treasury's offer and keep yields from inching up despite recent statements that the 1997 budget gap may push next year's 13 percent inflation target out of reach.

"The 950 million zloty offer will not be enough...(but) some may bid for lower prices after the central bank statements about inflationary effects of the 1997 budget," said Bartlomiej Kumela, senior dealer at Societe Generale in Warsaw.
Analysts said additional government spending, created by the larger 1997 budget gap, would likely require the treasury to increase its offers and keep yields underpinned next year.

They said foreign investors were likely to remain passive on Monday despite the central bank's forecast that in 1997 the zloty would likely be devalued by nine percent against the basket of currencies, down from some 12.7 percent this year. @

"Yields will hold relatively flat on Monday as the market awaits for the return of foreigners following the zloty slower devaluation news, but this is not likely to happen on Monday" said one dealer at a foreign bank here.

Analysts said foreigners were likely waiting for the central bank to be more precise about how far it wants year-on-year inflation to drop before it will cut the zloty devaluation rate, presently at one percent per month.
Inflation, at year-on-year 19.5 percent in September, is expected to fall to 18.7 in December and 16.6 in October 1997.
At Monday's auction the average yield for the benchmark 52-week bill was seen flat at this week's 19.46 percent, and just up at 19.15 percent for the 26-week paper.
The shortest 13-week T-bill yield was expected to hold flat at 18.55 or ease under heavy demand from corporate clients.
The treasury will offer 550 million of the benchmark, and 200 million of the 26- and 13-week bills on Monday.
The zloty was expected to hold at present levels between 1.7 and 1.9 percent from the trading band centre next week unless foreign investors become active in Polish treasuries, analysts said.
The zloty closed the week at 1.81 percent from parity after tracking volatile dollar/mark for most of the past week.
They said turnover on the forex market remained thin and that most transactions were done at the daily post-trade fixing with the central bank.

Analysts said most banks were going into the last week of the money market's October reserve period with a cash surplus and that one-day rates would ease next week unless the central bank drained the market.

"The central bank is likely to roll over about a billion zlotys from maturing operations early next week and this may keep trade balanced and prevent falls in interbank rates," said Krzysztof Poznanski, a dealer at WBK SA.
On Friday one-day rates closed around the Polish market's main 14-day drainage rate of 19.14 percent.
